Title:MASSAGE ESTABLISHMENTS BILL
MPs Speaking:Mr K. M. Byrne (Minister for Labour and Law); Dr Lee Siew Choh; Inche Buang Bin Omar Junid; Sir George Oehlers (Mr Speaker);


Column: 609

MASSAGE ESTABLISHMENTS BILL


    Dr Lee Siew Choh (Queenstown): Mr Speaker, Sir, like most things that will forever look for the line of least resistance, so we see so many massage establishments mushrooming all over Singapore. Those who read Chinese newspapers no doubt will see daily advertisements which show pretty faces and also tell prospective clients where to go for a pleasant massage. But in medical practice, Sir, massage is a form of treatment advocated for the loosening of stiff joints and tired muscles [Laughter] and helping - excuse me, Sir - to promote a free blood flow [Laughter] to the affected parts, thus increasing [Laughter] - sorry, Sir - the outflow of waste products and generally stimulating the activity of the human body. But of course the snag is that there are many parts of the body [Laughter]-

    Mr Speaker: Order. I think probably the Member for Queenstown is anticipating a pleasant massage after this sitting!
